function.uniprot_function: Key downstream component of the canonical Wnt signaling pathway. In the absence of Wnt, forms a complex with AXIN1, AXIN2, APC, CSNK1A1 and GSK3B that promotes phosphorylation on N-terminal Ser and Thr residues and ubiquitination of CTNNB1 via BTRC and its subsequent degradation by the proteasome. In the presence of Wnt ligand, CTNNB1 is not ubiquitinated and accumulates in the nucleus, where it acts as a coactivator for transcription factors of the TCF/LEF family, leading to activation of Wnt responsive genes. Involved in the regulation of cell adhesion, as component of an E-cadherin:catenin adhesion complex. Acts as a negative regulator of centrosome cohesion. Blocks anoikis of malignant kidney and intestinal epithelial cells and promotes their aggregation.
function.catalytic_activity: Non-enzymatic; functions as structural and signaling adapter protein
function.tissue_specificity: Broadly expressed in multiple tissues including colon epithelium, hair follicles, and throughout developing embryo. Particularly important in tissues with high Wnt signaling activity and epithelial homeostasis

pathways.pathway_role_summary: Beta-catenin is the central effector of canonical Wnt signaling. In the absence of Wnt, it is sequentially phosphorylated by CK1 (Ser45) and GSK3B (Thr41, Ser37, Ser33) within the destruction complex organized by AXIN1/2 and APC, leading to beta-TrCP-mediated ubiquitination (at Lys19/Lys49) and proteasomal degradation. Phosphorylation-dependent APC binding (300-fold affinity increase when phosphorylated, Kd ~2-10 nM vs 0.6-3.1 μM) is critical for efficient destruction complex function. Upon Wnt binding to FZD/LRP5/6 receptors, the destruction complex is inhibited, beta-catenin accumulates and translocates to the nucleus where it binds TCF/LEF transcription factors (via ARM repeats 3-9, salt bridges with Lys312/Lys435) to activate target genes controlling proliferation, differentiation, and stem cell maintenance. Beta-catenin also functions independently of Wnt signaling as a structural component of adherens junctions, linking E-cadherin (Kd ~85 nM) to the actin cytoskeleton via alpha-catenin (Kd ~15 nM).

disease_associations.description: Activating mutations in exon 3 affecting Ser33, Ser37, Thr41, or Ser45 prevent phosphorylation-dependent degradation, leading to constitutive Wnt signaling. Common mutations include Ser45 deletion/missense and Ser33 to Tyr substitution. Found in up to 25% of colorectal cancers.
Frequent CTNNB1 mutations including Ser45 to Phe or Pro substitutions, and Thr41 mutations. CTNNB1 mutations associated with favorable clinical outcomes and longer time to recurrence in HCC patients.
Mutations in exon 3 degradation targeting box lead to accumulation of beta-catenin, particularly in WNT-subgroup medulloblastomas with excellent prognosis.

metadata.data_quality_notes: Comprehensive quantitative data available for APC binding affinity with dramatic phosphorylation-dependence (Kd 2-10 nM phosphorylated vs 600-3100 nM unphosphorylated, ~300-fold difference). GSK3B kinetic parameters well-characterized (Km ~8.5 μM, kcat ~0.079/sec for catalytic domain). Individual ARM repeat boundaries based on PROSITE annotations and structural literature (~42 residues each). Direct Kd values for AXIN1, TCF7L2/LEF1, and beta-TrCP not quantitatively characterized in accessible literature - these interactions studied via co-IP and structural methods. E-cadherin binding Kd estimated from plakoglobin homology data (~85 nM). Alpha-catenin binding well-characterized at 15 nM. PTM sites extensively documented with 15+ phosphorylation sites across Ser/Thr/Tyr residues. Sequential phosphorylation cascade mechanism well-established with strict Ser45 priming requirement.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: Beta-catenin is the central node of canonical Wnt signaling and critical target for cancer therapy modeling. Key quantitative parameters for pathway modeling: (1) Sequential phosphorylation cascade (CK1→GSK3B) with well-defined kinetics (Km ~8.5 μM, kcat ~0.079/sec); (2) Destruction complex assembly via AXIN1 provides ~2-fold catalytic enhancement; (3) Phosphorylation-dependent APC binding shows dramatic 300-fold affinity increase (Kd 2-10 nM vs 0.6-3.1 μM), rate-limiting for destruction complex function; (4) 12 ARM repeats (residues 141-664) create extended binding groove with specific binding determinants (Lys312 in ARM5, Lys435 in ARM8) for multiple overlapping partners; (5) Nuclear vs cytoplasmic partitioning controlled by phosphorylation state and competitive binding; (6) Dual function in cell adhesion (E-cadherin ~85 nM, alpha-catenin ~15 nM) vs transcription (TCF/LEF) creates functional compartmentalization; (7) Disease-relevant mutations at destruction box (Ser33/Ser37/Thr41/Ser45) provide constitutive activation phenotypes. Quantitative binding and kinetic data enables mechanistic rule-based modeling of destruction complex dynamics, Wnt-induced stabilization, and therapeutic intervention strategies.
